title: There is an SCP file with your name on it
dek: No wiki diving needed. Twelve questions and the Foundation will decide whether you get a room, a corridor, or four pages of redactions.

options.label: A photograph nobody can look at directly
A medical note written in a very old hand
A request for more space and better food
Four pages of redactions and a blank cover
Keep the door closed. That's it. That's the procedure.
Do not look at it. Do not think about it.
Give it a room, a routine and something to do
Measure the space. It keeps growing.
A locked box with a very simple rule
A corridor that will not end
A corridor with one door at the far end
options.alt: A dark corridor leading to a closed door

options.label: A room with too much medical equipment in it
options.alt: An empty hospital corridor with pale lighting

options.label: A very large shop with no exits marked
A bright room with a table bolted to the floor
options.alt: A large, brightly lit laboratory room

questions.helper: Across: it hides or it hunts. Up: very old or brand new.

questions.prompt: Rank what the Foundation tries first.
questions.helper: First place is the step you'd insist on.
Two gaps. The second one is the important one.
questions.template: The file says {a}. Under no circumstances {b}.

options.label: the object is a statue that moves when unobserved
the object claims to cure what it caused
the object is friendly, and that is the anomaly

questions.prompt: I am very hard to get rid of.
questions.low: One good reason and I'm gone

questions.prompt: Fear is a more honest response than comfort.
The scariest thing is a space that keeps going.

options.label: "It was in a different position."
"It was already inside."
"It hugged the researcher."
"The report has been deleted."

questions.prompt: The note in the margin, in the researcher's handwriting:

options.label: "Do not blink."
"It was kind. That's what worries me."
"It knows the building better than we do."
"I have been walking for six hours."

results.name: SCP-173 — THE SCULPTURE
results.tagline: Object class: Euclid. Rule: keep looking
results.blurb: You are perfectly still until someone stops paying attention, and then you have already moved. People describe you as low-maintenance and easy to contain, right up until the moment they blink. You do not need to be understood. You need to be watched, continuously, by at least two people.
results.watchOut: You act the moment attention drifts. Say something before people look away.

results.name: SCP-049 — THE PLAGUE DOCTOR
results.tagline: Object class: Euclid. The cure is worse
results.blurb: You are certain you are helping. That is the whole problem. You diagnose people in the first five minutes, you have a treatment plan they did not ask for, and your bedside manner is strangely gentle for someone about to make everything considerably worse.
results.watchOut: Not everyone wants your cure. Ask before you operate.

results.name: SCP-096 — THE SHY GUY
results.tagline: Object class: Euclid. Do not look at the face
results.blurb: You are quiet, unremarkable and entirely fine until somebody looks directly at the thing you keep hidden. Then it is a very long, very fast, very loud problem and there is no reasoning with you. You are not dangerous in general. You are dangerous specifically.
results.watchOut: One perceived intrusion and you go all the way. Build a warning system that isn't rage.

results.name: SCP-106 — THE OLD MAN
results.tagline: Object class: Keter. It comes through the wall
results.blurb: You arrive without warning, in a place nobody expected, and you take things that do not come back. You are patient in a way that unsettles people. You do not chase. You wait in a corridor until someone walks past, and then the corridor is yours.
results.watchOut: You take more than you mean to. Give something back this week.

results.name: SCP-999 — THE TICKLE MONSTER
results.tagline: Object class: Safe. Approach without fear
results.blurb: You are the anomaly that helps: orange, warm, inexplicably comforting, and capable of improving the mood of an entire facility. Nobody can explain you and nobody wants to. The Foundation keeps you because you are the only thing in the building that makes the other files bearable.
results.watchOut: You give comfort to people who never ask how you are. Let someone check on you.

results.name: SCP-682 — THE HARD-TO-DESTROY REPTILE
results.tagline: Object class: Keter. Termination attempts: ongoing
results.blurb: You have survived every attempt to remove you from the situation, including several that should have worked. You are not especially nice about it. You adapt, you regenerate, and you make it extremely clear that whatever the plan was, you are still here and still unimpressed.
results.watchOut: Surviving is not the same as thriving. Let something soften you.

results.name: SCP-3008 — THE INFINITE RETAIL SPACE
results.tagline: Object class: Euclid. No exits. Furniture available.
results.blurb: You are an endless, well-lit, aggressively normal place that people wander into and cannot leave. Everything is arranged, everything is labelled, and there is no way out, only more aisles. You are not hostile. You are just structurally impossible to finish.
results.watchOut: You keep people so comfortable they forget to leave. Let them find a door.

results.name: SCP-055 — THE ANTI-MEME
results.tagline: Object class: Keter. Description: not what you think
results.blurb: You are the thing everyone forgets, including the people who wrote you down. You are not invisible. You are unmemorable, which is worse, because people meet you, like you, and then cannot say a single thing about you afterwards. Your file exists. Nobody can summarise it.
results.watchOut: Being unforgettable takes effort for you. Send the follow-up message.

results.name: SCP-087 — THE STAIRWELL
results.tagline: Object class: Euclid. It goes down further than it should
results.blurb: You are a descent: dim, concrete, and always one more flight than you expected. People go down to help and keep going. You are not malicious. You are just deeper than anyone planned for, and you make a very specific sound when someone stops to listen.
results.watchOut: You keep going down when you should turn around. Set a floor.
